spec.name: Reversal v10
spec.notes: Short-horizon reversal: buy yesterday's losers, sell the winners.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.6, annual return 9%, maximum drawdown 3%.

exhibits.summary: On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is -6.11 against 2.60 in research, a gap of +8.71.
Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.60 to -4.99 (change -7.59).

charges.argument: The strategy exhibits severe look-ahead bias, as the Sharpe ratio collapses from 2.60 to -4.99 when a one-bar delay is introduced.
The strategy failed the holdout test completely, with the Sharpe ratio dropping from 2.60 in research to -6.11 in the sealed period, indicating significant overfitting.

rebuttals.argument: The collapse in Sharpe ratio upon introducing a one-bar delay confirms that the strategy relies on information not available at the time of execution.
The significant negative performance in the holdout period confirms that the research-period results were the product of severe overfitting rather than a robust predictive edge.

verdict.opinion: The strategy is fundamentally flawed. The concession of lookahead bias, confirmed by the catastrophic performance drop in EX-2 when a one-bar delay is introduced, proves the research results are non-executable. Furthermore, the holdout test in EX-1 shows a complete collapse in performance, moving from a Sharpe of 2.6 to -6.11. This indicates severe overfitting and a lack of any genuine predictive edge. Given the reliance on lookahead bias and the failure to generalize to out-of-sample data, this strategy is rejected to prevent capital loss.
